featured_reviews.name: Naveed Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text: The Book Shop in Vile Parle East has been a quiet constant in my life for as long as I can remember. I’ve been visiting it since childhood, hand in hand with my father, when a good book and a peaceful afternoon felt like the perfect reward. Today, I walk those same paths with my wife, hoping that one day my child will do the same. There’s something timeless about this place—an old-world charm that refuses to fade. Books spill out onto the pavement, from classics and self-help to academic treasures, many of them second-hand and priced at a fraction of their worth. I’ve never walked away empty-handed; somehow, I always find a title that speaks to me. The affordability is a gift, especially when so much around us keeps getting more expensive. That said, I’ve heard whispers—and felt a hint myself—of the staff being a little curt or unwelcoming at times. It doesn’t happen often, but it’s there. The store itself is a treasure trove—beautifully lit, impeccably clean, and so well-organized that you feel welcomed the moment you step inside. It’s clear a lot of care goes into curating the selection. They have an incredible range of books for every age group, from whimsical children's picture books to thought-provoking literary fiction including a delightful collection of sacred artefacts, tarot cards, and other unique items interspersed throughout. It gives the place a very special, almost magical atmosphere.

While i was busy browsing through the sections of my interest, without being  intrusive in the slightest; Mr Shubham Mishra simply observed from a respectful distance, clearly trying to gauge my interests without disturbing my flow. It was a subtle art—distant, unobtrusive observation—and it was incredibly effective.

After a few minutes, he politely approached. Without any pressure or small talk, he simply said, "If you're interested in that author, you might also appreciate these," and gently placed a set of related books on a table besides me .They were all perfect suggestions, one that showed he truly understood the theme I was exploring.

Then, he did something I wish every bookseller would do: he simply , smiled, and vanished  as quietly as he had appeared giving  me the needed space and silence to browse through the books, to read the first few pages, and to decide for myself if it was the right fit. There was no hovering, no sales pitch—just expert guidance delivered with the utmost respect for the reader's private journey.

This level of attentive, intelligent, and graceful service is incredibly rare. He didn't just sell me the books; he enhanced my entire experience and deepened my love for browsing physical bookstores.

If you're looking for a perfect book or a unique gift in a serene and welcoming environment,with sincere expertise and assistance of Mr Shubham Mishra ,do yourself a favor and visit [Granth The Booktore at Taj Santacruz , Mumbai I know I'll be back.
